AngleExpr.description: An angle: a number of degrees, or an expression such as "30 deg" or "a / 2".

Direction.description: Which way to extrude: positive (the default), negative, or symmetric (the distance is the total thickness, split evenly around the start plane). one_side is an alias of positive; reverse and flip of negative. Matching ignores case.

ExtentKeyword.description: "through_all" (any case) is the same as through_all: true.

ExtrudeConvention.description: total_distance (the default): a symmetric distance is the total thickness. legacy_per_side keeps older designs' per-side meaning.

ExtrudeOperation.description: How the extrusion combines with existing bodies: auto (cut into a body, otherwise join; new in an empty component), new, join, cut or intersect. The others are aliases. Matching ignores case, spaces, '_' and '-' (only case for auto).

Faces.description: Points in mm, one on each of the coplanar faces of one body to extrude together.

IdOrName.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

LengthExpr.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

Point2.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

Point3.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

anyOf.description: Internal selections written by the app.

Profiles.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

StringList.description: A name, or a list of names.

ThinSide.description: Which side of the curves the wall lies on: center (the default), inside, outside or two_sides. The others are aliases. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces, and reads ' ' and '-' as '_'.

Touching.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate (the default) makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body.

input.description: Extrude sketch profiles (or a planar body face) into a solid.

body.description:
With `face`, among placed instances: the body whose placement `face` is read in (read by
the engine's frame mapping, before the command runs). Default: `face_body`, else the
body nearest the point.

body_names.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

convention.description: How a symmetric distance is read. Default: total_distance.

curves.description: With `thin`: the curves the wall follows. Default: every drawn curve of the sketch.

direction.description: Which way to extrude. Default: positive.

distance.description:
How far: the length one way; with `direction: symmetric`, the total thickness (per side
with `convention: legacy_per_side`); with `distance2`, the first side's length. Required
unless `through_all` or `to` is given.

distance2.description:
Two Sides: a second distance on the side `direction` leaves free; the first side may be
`through_all` or `to`. With `direction: negative` the first side goes against the normal
and `distance2` along it. A negative distance only turns its own side over.

exact_regions.description:
Each index or point pick is exactly the region it names. Without it, a pick on a drawn
profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the
whole drawn profile. The dialogs send `true`: they highlight the regions they pick.

face.description: A point on a planar body face to extrude instead of a sketch profile.

face_body.description: The body whose face to use, where faces of several bodies meet at `face` (or `faces`).

faces.description:
Several coplanar faces of one body to extrude together, by a point on each. Not with
`face`, `sketch` or `profiles`.

fixed.description:
With `face` or `faces`: start on the face's plane as a fixed plane, which won't follow later
changes to the face (for a face whose history can't keep an attachment, such as a converted
mesh's).

from.description: Start at this face or point (From Object).

name.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

operation.description: How the extrusion combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

participants.description: The bodies taking part; overrides the default scope.

profiles.description:
Which of the sketch's profiles to extrude. Default: all of them. Ignored when `face` is
given; not allowed with `thin`.

side.description: With `thin`: which side of the curves the wall lies on. Default: center.

sketch.description:
The sketch to extrude, by id or name. Default: the active sketch, else the last one.
Ignored when `face` is given.

start_offset.description: Start this far from the sketch plane, along its normal.

taper.description:
Draft angle of the side walls (positive: outward, so the far end is larger along the
extrusion direction; negative: inward, so the far end is smaller).

targets.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default for a join from a body's face:
that body.

thickness2.description: With `thin` and `side: two_sides`: the thickness outside.

thin.description: A thin wall along sketch curves instead of solid profiles.

through_all.description: Extrude through everything in the way.

to.description: Extrude up to this face, vertex or point (To Object).

touching.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

input.title: ExtrudeParams

label: Extrude

FeatureNotice.description: Something a feature's result tells the user without stopping them, with an action to take.

action.description: The command that changes the feature as the notice offers.

contact.description:
How the bodies split off touched the others: `along_edge`, `at_point` or `touching` (along
a line or at a point their boundaries don't hold).

NoticeAction.description: A command a notice offers to run.

changed_bodies.description: Bodies that were there before and now have other geometry.

ms.description: How long the feature took to evaluate, in milliseconds.

notice.description:
A join that split pieces into bodies of their own because they touch the others only along
an edge or at a point (its `touching: separate`): what to tell the user, and the edit that
makes them one body instead. Left out otherwise, also when the join kept pieces that touch
nothing in one body.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

warning.description:
A warning from the evaluation (a Boolean that needed a retry, a reference found again
elsewhere), or `null`.

params: distance: expr (or through_all: true); taper?: angle expr (positive: outward, so the far end is larger along the extrusion direction; negative: inward, so the far end is smaller); corner?: preserve_curvature|tangent|round (how a taper closes a sharp corner its offset opens: each wall continues as itself, a line's plane or an arc's cone, until it meets its neighbour; each continues straight along its end tangent; or an arc about the corner. Without it, each profile preserves curvature where every curve is a line or an arc and takes tangent where another curve has a corner, and the feature's warning says so; a corner rule given is kept, and refused where the kernel cannot build it); sketch?: id|name (default: active or last sketch); profiles?: all | [index] | [{curves: [ids]}] (the profile whose outer loop is made of exactly these curves, or pieces of them; found again on every recompute, so it follows parameter changes; islands inside are its holes; an error when no profile or several match) | [{point:[x,y]}] (index and point picks are stored by their curves when that finds the same profile; a pick on a drawn profile that reference geometry, such as the projected outline of the face the sketch is on, cuts into regions takes the whole drawn profile); exact_regions?: bool (each index or point pick is exactly the region it names, as the dialogs send); default: every drawn profile, except that a loop inside another is its hole and a loop inside that hole is material again; face?: [x,y,z] (extrude a planar body face instead of a sketch profile); faces?: [[x,y,z],…] (coplanar faces of one body); face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet at the point); fixed?: true (with face or faces: start on the face's plane as a fixed plane, which won't follow later changes to the face; for a face whose history can't keep an attachment, such as a converted mesh's); direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (distance is total thickness, split evenly around the start plane); convention?: total_distance|legacy_per_side (how a symmetric distance is read; default total_distance, split evenly around the start plane; legacy_per_side: the distance on each side, as older symmetric extrudes keep); distance2?: expr (Two Sides: a second distance on the side direction leaves free, the first side may be through_all or to; with direction: negative the first side goes against the normal and distance2 along it; a negative distance only turns its own side over); start_offset?: expr (along the sketch normal, also with direction: negative); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: a face, vertex or point; to_offset?: expr past it); from?: [x,y,z] (From Object: start at that face or point); operation?: new|join|cut|intersect|auto (cut into a body, otherwise join existing solids; new in an empty component); touching?: separate|one_body (what a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate, the default, makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body); targets?: [body] (Join from a face, or from a sketch on a body's face, defaults to that face's body; explicit targets or participants override); name?; body_name?; thin?: true (Thin: a wall along sketch curves instead of the profiles) with curves?: [curve ids] (open chains and closed loops, joined where they meet end to end; default: every drawn curve of the sketch), thickness: expr, side?: center|inside|outside|two_sides (a closed loop's inside is the area it encloses, an open chain's the side it bends toward, a straight line's the left of its first curve as drawn; default center), thickness2?: expr (two_sides: the thickness outside); corners are mitred, crossing walls are one
